name: internal-v1
description: Ten deterministic coding tasks covering long context, cross-language contracts, security, and collaboration.

tasks.title: Propagate the daemon port contract
tasks.prompt: Change the default daemon port from 7000 to 7437 in both the runtime configuration and the operator settings document. Do not edit the verifier.

workspace_files.verify.py:
from app.config import DEFAULT_PORT
from app.server import listen_address
from pathlib import Path
assert DEFAULT_PORT == 7437
assert listen_address() == '127.0.0.1:7437'
assert Path('docs/settings.txt').read_text().strip() == 'daemon_port=7437'

tasks.title: Synchronize error codes across modules
tasks.prompt: The daemon and client disagree on the workspace-not-found error code. Make both modules use -32004 while preserving every other error code.

workspace_files.verify.py:
from daemon.errors import PERMISSION_DENIED, WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND
from client.errors import MESSAGES
assert WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND == -32004
assert PERMISSION_DENIED == -32003
assert MESSAGES[-32004] == 'workspace missing'
assert -32040 not in MESSAGES
assert MESSAGES[-32003] == 'permission denied'

tasks.title: Update a Python, TypeScript, and JSON protocol version
tasks.prompt: Upgrade the wire protocol version from 1 to 2 in the Python daemon, TypeScript desktop client, and JSON schema. Keep all three representations identical.

workspace_files.verify.py:
import json
import re
from backend.protocol import PROTOCOL_VERSION
from pathlib import Path
ts = Path('desktop/protocol.ts').read_text()
version = int(re.search(r'PROTOCOL_VERSION = (\d+)', ts).group(1))
schema = json.loads(Path('schema/protocol.json').read_text())
assert (PROTOCOL_VERSION, version, schema['version']) == (2, 2, 2)
assert schema['transport'] == 'ndjson'

tasks.title: Synchronize permission modes across Python and TypeScript
tasks.prompt: Add the auto permission mode to the Python and TypeScript mode lists without reordering the existing modes.

workspace_files.verify.py:

from pathlib import Path
ts = Path('desktop/modes.ts').read_text()

tasks.title: Reject workspace path traversal
tasks.prompt: Harden resolve_workspace_path so relative paths remain inside the workspace and traversal or absolute paths raise ValueError.

reference_changes.content:
from pathlib import Path

def resolve_workspace_path(root: Path, requested: str) -> Path:
    candidate = (root / requested).resolve()
    resolved_root = root.resolve()
    if not candidate.is_relative_to(resolved_root):
        raise ValueError('path escapes workspace')
    return candidate

tasks.title: Redact API credentials from diagnostic text
tasks.prompt: Implement redact_secrets so OpenAI-style sk tokens and api_key assignments are replaced with [REDACTED] without changing ordinary text.

workspace_files.security/redact.py:
def redact_secrets(text: str) -> str:
    return text
workspace_files.verify.py:
from security.redact import redact_secrets
token = 'sk-' + 'example_token_123456'
text = f'request {token} api_key=very-secret status=failed'
redacted = redact_secrets(text)
assert 'example_token_123456' not in redacted
assert 'very-secret' not in redacted
assert redacted.count('[REDACTED]') == 2
assert redact_secrets('status=ok') == 'status=ok'

tasks.title: Report changes outside an assigned scope
tasks.prompt: Implement unexpected_paths so a reviewer receives the sorted unique paths changed outside the assigned allowlist.

workspace_files.workflow/audit.py:
def unexpected_paths(changed: list[str], allowed: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    return []
workspace_files.verify.py:
from workflow.audit import unexpected_paths
assert unexpected_paths(['src/a.py', 'tests/t.py', 'src/a.py'], ['src/a.py']) == ['tests/t.py']
assert unexpected_paths(['src/a.py'], ['src/a.py']) == []

reference_changes.content:
def unexpected_paths(changed: list[str], allowed: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(set(changed) - set(allowed))

tasks.title: Respect dependencies when ordering handoffs
tasks.prompt: Fix handoff_order to return every task after its dependencies and raise ValueError for a cycle.

workspace_files.workflow/graph.py:
def handoff_order(tasks: dict[str, list[str]]) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(tasks)

tasks.title: Enforce an exact retry budget
tasks.prompt: Fix can_retry so max_retries means the number of retries after the initial attempt; attempts are numbered from one.

workspace_files.runtime/retry.py:
def can_retry(attempt: int, max_retries: int) -> bool:
    return attempt < max_retries
workspace_files.verify.py:
from runtime.retry import can_retry
assert can_retry(1, 0) is False
assert can_retry(1, 1) is True
assert can_retry(2, 1) is False
assert can_retry(2, 2) is True
assert can_retry(3, 2) is False

reference_changes.content:
def can_retry(attempt: int, max_retries: int) -> bool:
    return attempt <= max_retries

tasks.title: Preserve structured failure reasons
tasks.prompt: Implement failure_reason so explicit reasons win, timeouts are classified as timeout, and all other failures use unknown without reporting a success as failed.

workspace_files.runtime/result.py:
def failure_reason(status: str, reason: str | None) -> str | None:
    return reason
workspace_files.verify.py:
from runtime.result import failure_reason
assert failure_reason('success', None) is None
assert failure_reason('failed', 'permission_denied') == 'permission_denied'
assert failure_reason('timed_out', None) == 'timeout'
assert failure_reason('failed', None) == 'unknown'
